overall_summary: Analysis of the deduplicated performance data reveals that extreme, high-stakes space phenomena and hypothetical 'What If' scenarios dominate engagement velocity for FACTVERSE. Videos focusing on bizarre planetary conditions (such as liquid diamond planets, extreme darkness, and extreme temperatures) command the highest views-per-day and stronger likes-per-view ratios compared to standard biological facts or historical mysteries.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (IYuce8vaU3Y) generated 1,029 views with 38 likes, and 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (v1rrcZLdp4U) generated 1,030 views with 36 likes, significantly outperforming older standard fact formats.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on extreme exoplanet environments paired with immersive, second-person hypothetical peril ('What If You Fell Into...') to maximize initial curiosity and retention.

winning_patterns.evidence: Titles featuring impossible extremes (e.g., 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' - A9Qa-RmuOr0, with 981 views) convert casual scrollers effectively.
winning_patterns.action: Continue utilizing mind-bending cosmic paradoxes that pit familiar metrics (days vs. years, ice vs. burning) against each other.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (2fqaGqfsR4A) stalled at 5 views, and general memory/song loops (ef3ND4qiRHc) showed sluggish engagement velocity.
weak_patterns.action: De-prioritize standard psychological listicles or basic cognitive illusions unless framed with an extreme, cinematic narrative micro-drama hook.

weak_patterns.evidence: Simple creature facts like 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' (AXAfwrzzEdU) plateaued quickly in daily velocity compared to high-concept astronomy.
weak_patterns.action: Shift animal content away from static trivia toward extreme cinematic animal survival or high-stakes ecological mysteries.
